extracted.intended_audience: aspiring patent agents and IP professionals in Singapore preparing to register or sit the Patent Agents Qualifying Examination (QE)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility, fee structure, preparatory guidance, and administrative instructions for enrolling in and attempting the Patent Agents Qualifying Examination (QE) in Singapore. Covers pre-requisites, module-to-paper mappings, attempt-counting and fees, document requirements, and preparatory recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-requisite for QE enrolment
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who wishes to enrol for the QE must first meet one of the following pre-requisites: a) Passed the Graduate Certificate in Intellectual Property Law course (GCIP) conducted by the Faculty of Law, National University of Singapore; b) Passed the modules under the Graduate Diploma in IP and Innovation Management (GDIPIM) or Master of IP and Innovation Management (MIPIM) conducted by the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) that correspond to the QE paper(s) they are enrolling in; c) Obtained approval from the Registrar to be exempted from complying with the requirement set out in Rule 6 of the Patents (Patent Agents) Rules 2001 to have passed GCIP, GDIPIM or MIPIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the acceptable routes to satisfy the pre-requisite. Candidates who have already passed GCIP are not subject to the pre-requisite. For exemption under (c), applicants must obtain Registrar approval and submit documents showing equivalence. The page also provides an FAQ explanation of why the pre-requisite is implemented (to better prepare candidates).

rubrics_metrics.name: GDIPIM / MIPIM module mapping to QE papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific GDIPIM/MIPIM modules correspond to QE papers and satisfy the module-based pre-requisite: IPM527 – Patent Claims and IPM529 – Patent Applications → Paper A; IPM525 – Patent Office Action → Paper B; IPM531 – Patent Infringement and Validity → Paper C; IPM523 – Patent Practice in Singapore → Paper D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview table provided so candidates know which module(s) they must pass to enrol for each QE paper. The page also notes these modules may be taken as CET courses to prepare for QE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6(3) Patent Examiner pathway (7+ years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 6(3), an individual who has worked as a Patent Examiner in Singapore for at least 7 years and is pursuing registration is only required to pass QE Papers A and C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for Rule 6(3) candidates, the pre-requisite applies in relation to Papers A and C: they must pass the corresponding GDIPIM/MIPIM modules (IPM527/IPM529 for Paper A; IPM531 for Paper C) before enrolling for those papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence required for enrolment
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents to show that candidates have passed the relevant course/module(s) (e.g., official transcript, notification of results from the school) must be submitted to enrol for QE. For candidates currently taking modules, documents showing they have passed must be submitted by specified deadlines (e.g., by 27 December 2022). For exemption applicants, documents to show they passed an equivalent course/module must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a candidate enrolls before final module results are available they should complete enrolment and submit the passing documents by the deadline. If the candidate subsequently does not pass the relevant module, they are entitled to a refund of the examination fee for that paper. FAQ entries clarify handling of in-progress module results and refunds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended practical preparation (internship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are encouraged to attempt QE only after undergoing a minimum of one-year internship in patent agency work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation, together with the modules, is intended to provide candidates with the knowledge and practical work experience to attempt QE. It is encouragement only and not a mandatory requirement; there is no requirement to attempt a particular combination of papers in one QE sitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2-Tier examination fee structure (amounts and tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2-Tier examination fee structure applies: Tier 1 (first to third attempt) — $642 per paper (inclusive of GST); Tier 2 (fourth and subsequent attempt) — $1,284 per paper (inclusive of GST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2-Tier structure was introduced in 2022 and is intended to encourage candidates to sit for the QE when sufficiently prepared. The page provides illustrations and worked examples showing how fees apply to different sequences of attempts across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and counting of 'attempts' (per paper, start date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'attempts' is an attempt at each subject paper (i.e., counted per paper). The revised counting only considers attempts per paper made starting from QE 2022 (held January 2023); any QE paper attempt prior to QE 2022 will not count as an attempt for the purposes of the revised 2-Tier fee structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worked examples and a comparative table show how historical attempts are treated under the current and revised fee structures, clarifying that a candidate's attempt count for each paper starts from QE 2022 and that Tier 2 fees are payable earliest at QE 2026 under the revised rules. Specific examples explain mixed scenarios (e.g., one paper reaching fourth attempt while another remains at second attempt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and SkillsFuture Credit eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: QE 2026 fees are eligible for SkillsFuture Credit as a base tier course for Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above who are self-funding their examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should consult the SkillsFuture website for detailed eligibility criteria and claim procedures. This provision helps eligible candidates manage the mandatory cost of the examination for patent agent qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of past papers and example passing scripts (caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Past papers and, since QE2022, examples of passing scripts are published for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important caveat: the scripts have not been revised for accuracy and should not be regarded as model answers. Candidates are referred to Examiner's Tips and FAQs for further preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrolment timing and combination of papers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that candidates need to attempt any particular combination of papers in one QE sitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may attempt papers across multiple QEs. The FAQs clarify that candidates who have passed most modules but are missing one (e.g., IPM523) may enrol for other papers if they have passed the corresponding modules; specific timing rules (submission deadlines for module pass evidence) apply.
